policy: Every seeded medical relationship has sourceRefs and an evidenceNote. Relationship predicates are intentionally conservative; graph paths must not be treated as proof of causation or individual diagnosis.

relationships.evidenceNote: Type 2 diabetes is a classified subtype of diabetes.
Prediabetes is a high-risk state for future Type 2 diabetes development; it does not imply that progression is inevitable.
Population evidence and reviews associate obesity with increased Type 2 diabetes risk. This is not a patient-specific diagnosis or proof of causation in an individual.
BMI is commonly used to screen for and classify overweight/obesity; it is a proxy measure and does not directly measure adiposity.
Reviews describe mechanisms linking excess adiposity and altered adipose tissue function with insulin resistance.
Insulin resistance is one contributor to Type 2 diabetes pathophysiology; it is not the only mechanism.
HbA1c is one measure used to assess glycaemic status; it must be interpreted with patient context and limitations.
A1C is one accepted laboratory criterion for diabetes diagnosis when performed and interpreted under the applicable guideline.
Fasting plasma glucose is one accepted plasma-glucose criterion for diagnosis, subject to confirmatory testing and clinical context.
Postprandial glucose can provide additional information when assessing glycaemic management.
Glycated albumin may be considered as an alternative validated biomarker in selected monitoring situations; it is not interchangeable with A1C in every context.
CGM provides repeated glucose measurements over time and supports interpretation of glucose patterns.
Capillary blood glucose is a method for measuring blood glucose; interpretation depends on timing and clinical context.
Mean glucose is a standard CGM-derived metric for a defined monitoring period.
Time in range is derived from CGM values and must specify the glucose range and analysis window.
Time below range is derived from CGM values using a specified glucose threshold and analysis window.
Time above range is derived from CGM values using a specified glucose threshold and analysis window.
GMI is calculated from mean CGM glucose and approximates, but is not always equivalent to, laboratory HbA1c.
CGM time-series values can be used to calculate glucose variability metrics.
Mean CGM glucose is one metric used in glycaemic-status assessment.
Time in range is one metric used in glycaemic-status assessment; goals depend on individual clinical context.
Time below range supports assessment of low-glucose exposure and hypoglycaemia risk.
Time above range supports assessment of elevated-glucose exposure.
GMI is a CGM-derived estimate related to average glucose; it should not be treated as an exact replacement for laboratory HbA1c.
Glucose variability is one aspect of CGM interpretation and should be considered alongside other metrics.
Measured glucose supports assessment and classification of hypoglycaemia when interpreted with the relevant guideline thresholds; v1 intentionally stores no numeric threshold.
Glucose measurements support assessment of hyperglycaemia; applicable thresholds depend on measurement setting and clinical context.
Ketone measurements support assessment of suspected ketoacidosis but do not diagnose DKA on their own.
Diabetic ketoacidosis is a type of acute hyperglycaemic crisis.
Type 2 diabetes is associated with microvascular complications; this general association does not imply an individual patient has a complication.
Type 2 diabetes is associated with macrovascular complications at a population/clinical level.
Chronic kidney disease is an important diabetes-associated condition and a focus of guideline-directed risk management.
eGFR is one measure used in kidney assessment; it should be interpreted with repeat testing, albuminuria and clinical context as appropriate.
Diabetic retinopathy is classified as a diabetes-related microvascular complication.
Diabetic neuropathy is classified among diabetes-related microvascular complications.
Diabetic nephropathy is classified as a diabetes-related microvascular complication.
Cardiovascular disease is represented as a macrovascular complication category in this simplified clinical ontology.
Insulin participates in physiological glucose regulation; treatment effects depend on formulation, dose, delivery and the individual.
Insulin is a treatment option for some people with Type 2 diabetes; this relationship does not recommend insulin for an individual patient.
Glucose-lowering medications are used in Type 2 diabetes management; choice must be individualized by a qualified clinician.
Dietary patterns and individualized nutrition are relevant to diabetes prevention and management; this edge does not prescribe a specific diet.
Physical activity is one element considered in Type 2 diabetes and weight-management care; individual goals should be personalized.
